prompt:
Some people think that parents should be mainly responsible for teaching children good behaviour and values. Others believe that schools should play the main role.

Discuss both these views and give your own opinion.

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Write at least 250 words.
checklist: Discuss the view that parents should be mainly responsible
Discuss the view that schools should play the main role
Give your own opinion clearly and consistently
Support both views with reasons and examples
Conclude with a summary of your position

for: Children spend their earliest and most formative years at home
Parents model behaviour every day; children copy what they see
Values such as religion or family traditions differ, and families have the right to pass on their own
Parents know their own child's personality and needs best
against: Many parents work long hours and have limited time with their children
School is where children learn to cooperate, share and respect people from different backgrounds
Teachers are trained professionals and can teach shared civic values consistently
Not all homes provide a positive example; school can compensate

models.text:
Opinions differ on whether the task of teaching children to behave well and develop sound values belongs primarily to families or to schools. While both institutions clearly have a part to play, I am convinced that parents carry the main responsibility, with schools reinforcing and extending what is learnt at home.

Those who believe schools should take the lead offer some convincing arguments. In many households both parents work full-time, so children may spend more of their waking hours with teachers than with their own mother and father. School is also the first place where most children must cooperate with large numbers of peers from different backgrounds, which makes it an ideal setting for learning tolerance, fairness and respect for rules. Moreover, not every home provides a positive model, and a good school can partly compensate for a chaotic or neglectful family environment.

Nevertheless, there are stronger reasons to regard the family as the primary influence. Children's characters are largely shaped in their first five or six years, long before formal education begins, and they learn above all by imitation. A child who regularly sees his parents apologise when they are wrong or treat shop assistants politely absorbs these habits far more deeply than he would from a lesson on good manners. Furthermore, values are closely tied to culture and belief, and it seems right that families should decide which traditions and principles they wish to pass on.

In my view, the most effective arrangement is a partnership in which parents set the foundations and schools build on them. Teachers can reinforce honesty, kindness and responsibility through daily routines, class discussions and school rules, but they cannot be expected to replace what is missing at home.

In conclusion, although schools make a valuable contribution to children's moral development, parents remain the most important teachers of behaviour and values, simply because their influence starts earlier and lasts longer.
models.commentary: Task Response (8): discute ambas posturas con argumentos sólidos y da una opinión clara (los padres tienen la responsabilidad principal, con la escuela como refuerzo) que se mantiene de principio a fin. Ejemplos concretos y bien integrados (pedir perdón, tratar con educación a los dependientes). Coherence & Cohesion (8): párrafos bien construidos; 'Nevertheless' marca el contraste con la postura más fuerte; buena referencia ('these habits', 'what is learnt at home'). Lexical Resource (8): léxico natural y preciso ('sound values', 'waking hours', 'compensate', 'neglectful', 'absorbs these habits', 'set the foundations'). Grammatical Range & Accuracy (8): estructuras variadas (comparativas, relativas, 'it seems right that...') sin errores. Para un 9: algo más de matiz (p. ej., qué ocurre cuando los valores de la familia chocan con los de la sociedad) y un ejemplo todavía más original.

models.text:
Children's behaviour and values are very important for the future of society. Some people believe that parents are mainly responsible for teaching these things, while others think that schools should do most of this work. In my opinion, parents have the most important role, but schools also need to help.

On the one hand, there are good reasons why schools should teach children how to behave. Nowadays, in many families both parents work long hours, so children spend most of the day at school. Teachers can teach children to respect others, to work in teams and to follow rules. For example, when students do group projects, they learn to listen to other people's opinions and to share responsibilities. These are skills that are difficult to learn at home.

On the other hand, parents have a stronger influence on their children. From a very young age, children copy the behaviour of their parents. If parents are polite and honest, their children will probably be the same. In addition, every family has its own culture and beliefs, and parents have the right to pass these values on to their children. Teachers have classes of thirty students, so they cannot pay attention to the behaviour of each child as carefully as parents can.

Personally, I believe that parents should be the main teachers of values, because children learn most from the people they love and live with. However, schools should support parents by teaching rules and cooperation in the classroom.

In conclusion, both parents and schools play a role in teaching children good behaviour, but parents have the main responsibility because their influence begins earlier and is stronger.
models.commentary: Task Response (7): discute ambas posturas y da una opinión clara y mantenida. El ejemplo del trabajo en grupo es útil; algunas afirmaciones son algo simples ('If parents are polite and honest, their children will probably be the same'). Coherence & Cohesion (7): organización lógica y clara, con conectores correctos aunque convencionales ('On the one hand', 'In addition', 'Personally', 'However'). Lexical Resource (7): vocabulario adecuado ('pass these values on', 'cooperation', 'share responsibilities'), con algo de repetición ('behaviour', 'values'). Grammatical Range & Accuracy (7): buen control de frases complejas y comparativas ('as carefully as parents can'); errores prácticamente ausentes. Para subir a 8: desarrollar los argumentos con más profundidad (por qué los primeros años son decisivos), usar léxico más preciso ('formative years', 'role model') y variar la forma de introducir las ideas.

models.text:
In the modern world, the behaviour of children is a big problem. Some people think that parents must teach the children good behaviour and values, but other people believe that it is the job of the school. I will discuss both views and give my opinion.

First, some people think that school is responsible. Children go to school every day and they spend there many hours. The teachers are professional and they know how to educate the children. Also in the school the children are with other children so they can learn to share and to respect. For example, if a child hit another child, the teacher can explain that this is wrong.

Second, other people think that parents are responsible. The parents are the first teachers of the children and the children copy everything that their parents do. If the parents shout or say bad words, the children will do the same. Also the parents know their children better than the teachers, because they live with them. In my country, the family is very important and the grandparents also help to educate the children.

In my opinion, I think that the parents are more responsible than the school. The school is for learn subjects like maths and science, not for teach values. But the teachers also can help a little bit if the children behave bad in the class.

In conclusion, both the parents and the school are important for the education of the children, but I think the parents has the main responsibility because they are with the children all their life.

La mención a los abuelos es una idea irrelevante para la pregunta. prompt:
In many countries, cash is being replaced by card and mobile phone payments, and some shops no longer accept notes and coins at all.

Do the advantages of this development outweigh the disadvantages?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Write at least 250 words.
checklist: Describe the main advantages of cashless payments
Describe the main disadvantages
State clearly whether the advantages outweigh the disadvantages (this is the actual question)
Support the ideas with explanation and examples
Keep the judgement consistent and restate it in the conclusion

for: Payments are faster and more convenient; no need to carry money or find change
Electronic transactions are traceable, making tax evasion and money laundering harder
Less cash means fewer robberies of shops and individuals
Businesses save the cost and risk of handling, counting and transporting cash
against: Elderly people, the poor and those without bank accounts may be excluded
Every purchase leaves a data trail, raising privacy concerns
Technical failures, power cuts or cyberattacks can stop all payments
People may overspend because digital money feels less 'real'

models.text:
In a growing number of countries, from Sweden to China, tapping a card or a smartphone has replaced handing over notes and coins, and some businesses now refuse cash altogether. While this shift brings substantial benefits, I believe its drawbacks are serious enough that the advantages outweigh them only if certain safeguards remain in place.

The benefits of digital payment are considerable. For consumers, it is undeniably convenient: there is no need to withdraw money, carry a heavy wallet or wait for change, and purchases can be made online or abroad without exchanging currency. For businesses, eliminating cash reduces the time spent counting takings and the risk of theft, both by robbers and by dishonest staff. Governments also gain, since electronic transactions leave a record, making it far harder to conceal income from the tax authorities or to launder the proceeds of crime.

However, the disadvantages fall disproportionately on the most vulnerable. Many elderly people are uncomfortable with smartphone apps, and some low-income citizens do not have a bank account at all; for them, a cashless shop is effectively a closed shop. Privacy is another concern, because a record of every purchase reveals a great deal about a person's habits, health and movements, information that could be misused by companies or governments. Finally, a society that relies entirely on electronic systems is exposed to technical failures: a network outage or cyberattack could leave people unable to buy food or medicine.

Weighing these points, I would argue that the advantages are greater, but only if cash continues to exist as a legal alternative. Several countries have already passed laws requiring essential services such as pharmacies and supermarkets to accept notes and coins, which seems a sensible compromise.

In conclusion, the move towards digital payment offers clear gains in convenience, security and transparency. Nevertheless, these benefits outweigh the costs only when the right to pay in cash is protected for those who need it.
models.commentary: Task Response (8): responde exactamente a la pregunta ('Do the advantages outweigh...?') con un juicio claro y matizado (sí, pero sólo si se protege el efectivo), presente en la introducción, en un párrafo de valoración y en la conclusión. Ventajas y desventajas bien desarrolladas para distintos actores (consumidores, empresas, Estado). Coherence & Cohesion (8): organización excelente; 'Weighing these points' introduce la valoración con naturalidad. Lexical Resource (8): léxico preciso ('takings', 'launder the proceeds of crime', 'disproportionately', 'network outage', 'sensible compromise'). Grammatical Range & Accuracy (8): estructuras complejas y variadas (punto y coma, participios, 'only if', relativas) sin errores. Para un 9: concretar con un caso real (p. ej., un apagón o un país concreto que legisló) y profundizar en alguna idea en lugar de enumerar tres desventajas.

models.text:
In recent years, more and more people pay with cards or mobile phones instead of cash, and in some countries certain shops do not accept cash anymore. In my opinion, the advantages of this trend are greater than the disadvantages, although some problems need to be solved.

The main advantage of cashless payments is convenience. People do not need to go to a cash machine or carry coins, and they can pay quickly by simply touching a card or phone on a machine. This is especially useful when travelling abroad, because there is no need to change money. Another benefit is safety. Since shops have less cash, they are less likely to be robbed, and people who lose their wallet can block their cards immediately. In addition, electronic payments are recorded, so it is more difficult for people to hide money from the government and avoid paying taxes.

On the other hand, there are some disadvantages. Older people often find it difficult to use new technology, so they may have problems when shops refuse cash. Similarly, poor people who do not have a bank account could be excluded. Furthermore, some people worry that banks and companies can see everything they buy, which is a threat to their privacy.

Overall, I believe that the benefits are more important, because they affect almost everyone in daily life, while the problems affect a smaller group of people. However, governments should make sure that cash is still accepted in essential places like supermarkets and pharmacies.

In conclusion, cashless payments make life easier and safer, so I think the advantages outweigh the disadvantages, as long as vulnerable people are protected.
models.commentary: Task Response (7): responde a la pregunta con una postura clara y la justifica ('affect almost everyone... a smaller group'), lo cual es un buen criterio de valoración. Las ideas son relevantes, aunque las desventajas se enumeran con poco desarrollo. Coherence & Cohesion (7): organización clara; conectores apropiados pero algo mecánicos ('Another benefit is', 'In addition', 'Similarly', 'Furthermore'). Lexical Resource (7): buen vocabulario ('convenience', 'block their cards', 'excluded', 'threat to their privacy'), aunque con algunas expresiones simples ('make life easier'). Grammatical Range & Accuracy (7): frases complejas correctas ('Since shops have less cash...', 'as long as'); prácticamente sin errores. Para subir a 8: desarrollar más cada desventaja con un ejemplo o consecuencia concreta, añadir un argumento menos obvio (dependencia tecnológica, ciberataques) y usar léxico más preciso.

prompt:
International tourism is now reaching remote places such as mountain villages, rainforests and small islands that few outsiders visited in the past.

Do the advantages of this trend outweigh the disadvantages?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Write at least 250 words.
checklist: Explain the advantages of tourism in remote places (for local people and/or visitors)
Explain the disadvantages (environment, culture, local economy)
Give a clear judgement on whether the advantages outweigh the disadvantages
Support ideas with explanation and relevant examples
Keep the judgement consistent throughout

for: Tourism brings income and jobs to communities with few other economic options
Entrance fees and eco-tourism can fund the protection of wildlife and habitats
Better roads, electricity and health services may follow tourist investment
Cultural exchange increases understanding and can revive traditional crafts
against: Fragile ecosystems suffer from litter, erosion, pollution and disturbance of wildlife
Traditional culture may become a commercial performance for visitors
Profits often go to outside companies rather than local people
Prices for land, food and housing rise, and local people may be pushed out

models.text:
Cheaper flights and social media have opened up corners of the world that were once virtually inaccessible, from Himalayan villages to coral islands in the Pacific. Although this trend creates real economic opportunities, I would argue that, as it is currently managed in many places, its disadvantages slightly outweigh its advantages.

The case in favour rests largely on economics. Remote communities often have few sources of income beyond subsistence farming or fishing, and visitors who pay for guides, homestays and handicrafts can transform local livelihoods. In some cases, tourism also funds conservation: national parks in Costa Rica and Rwanda, for instance, use entrance fees to pay rangers and protect endangered species, giving local people a financial reason to preserve rather than exploit their environment. Contact with visitors can, moreover, encourage young people to value and maintain traditional skills that might otherwise disappear.

Unfortunately, these benefits are frequently undermined by the way tourism develops in practice. Ecosystems in such places tend to be fragile, and even modest numbers of visitors can cause erosion on mountain paths, damage to coral reefs and an accumulation of waste that small communities have no means of processing. Furthermore, much of the money generated never reaches local people; it is captured by international tour operators, airlines and hotel chains. Meanwhile, residents may face rising prices for land and food, and their customs risk being reduced to a performance staged for cameras.

The balance could certainly shift if visitor numbers were limited and communities retained control over development, as Bhutan has attempted by charging a substantial daily fee to every tourist. Without such measures, however, the costs are borne mainly by the very people and environments that attract visitors in the first place.

In conclusion, tourism in remote areas has the potential to benefit both hosts and guests, but in its present, largely unregulated form, I believe its drawbacks prevail. Careful regulation is essential if the advantages are to outweigh the harm.
models.commentary: Task Response (8): juicio claro y algo inesperado (las desventajas pesan ligeramente más 'as it is currently managed'), lo cual demuestra pensamiento crítico; se mantiene y se matiza con una condición (regulación). Ejemplos concretos y pertinentes (Costa Rica, Ruanda, Bután). Coherence & Cohesion (8): progresión impecable; 'Unfortunately, these benefits are frequently undermined' enlaza los párrafos de forma natural. Lexical Resource (8): vocabulario rico y preciso ('subsistence farming', 'livelihoods', 'endangered species', 'erosion', 'staged for cameras', 'borne by'). Grammatical Range & Accuracy (8): estructuras avanzadas ('if the advantages are to outweigh', condicional de segundo tipo, pasivas) sin errores. Para un 9: algo más de desarrollo del impacto cultural, que queda en una sola frase, y una conclusión ligeramente más concisa.

models.text:
Nowadays, more and more tourists travel to remote areas such as small islands, jungles and mountain villages. This trend has both positive and negative effects, but I believe that the advantages outweigh the disadvantages if tourism is managed carefully.

The biggest advantage is economic. In many remote places, people are poor and there are not many jobs. When tourists arrive, local people can work as guides, open small restaurants or sell traditional products. For example, in some villages in Peru, families rent rooms to tourists who want to walk to Machu Picchu, and this gives them an important extra income. In addition, governments often improve roads, electricity and hospitals in these areas because of tourism, which benefits local residents as well.

However, there are also some serious disadvantages. The most important is the damage to the environment. Large numbers of visitors produce rubbish and pollution, and they can disturb wild animals. Another problem is that local traditions may change. Sometimes traditional festivals become shows for tourists and lose their original meaning. Moreover, big foreign companies sometimes build hotels in these places and take most of the profits.

In my view, these problems can be reduced with good management. Governments can limit the number of visitors, charge entrance fees and use the money to protect nature. They can also support small local businesses instead of large international companies.

In conclusion, although tourism in remote places can harm the environment and local culture, I think its economic benefits are greater, especially if governments control it in a responsible way.
models.commentary: Task Response (7): responde a la pregunta con una posición clara y la condiciona a una buena gestión; el ejemplo de Perú es concreto. Sin embargo, el juicio se apoya sobre todo en la economía sin explicar por qué ésta pesa más que el daño ambiental. Coherence & Cohesion (7): estructura clara; conectores adecuados pero algo repetitivos ('In addition', 'Another problem', 'Moreover'). Lexical Resource (7): vocabulario adecuado ('extra income', 'disturb wild animals', 'entrance fees', 'profits'), con algunas expresiones generales ('serious disadvantages', 'good management'). Grammatical Range & Accuracy (7): buen control de estructuras complejas, errores casi inexistentes. Para subir a 8: justificar explícitamente por qué un lado pesa más, desarrollar el problema de que los beneficios no llegan a la población local y usar léxico más preciso ('fragile ecosystems', 'livelihoods').

models.text:
In the last years, many tourists go to remote places like islands, forests and mountains. Before, nobody visited these places but now they are very popular because of the internet and social media. In my opinion, this trend has more advantages than disadvantages.

Firstly, tourism is good for the economy of these places. The local people can earn money because the tourists buy food, souvenirs and pay for hotels. Also they can work as guides and show the nature to the tourists. In this way, the young people don't need to move to the cities to find a job. For example, in Thailand there are many small islands that live from the tourism.

Secondly, the tourists can learn about different cultures. When they visit a village in the mountains, they see how the people live and they understand that there are different ways of life. This is very interesting and good for the tourists.

On the other hand, there are some disadvantages. The tourists can damage the nature, for example they throw rubbish in the beach or in the forest. Also, when there are too much tourists, the local people are not happy because the prices go up and there is a lot of noise. The traditional culture can also change because of the tourism.

In conclusion, I think that tourism in remote places is positive because it brings money and jobs to the local people. However, the government have to protect the nature and control the number of tourists so the problems are not very big.

prompt:
In some countries, it is common for young people to take a year off between finishing school and starting university, in order to work or travel.

Do the advantages of this outweigh the disadvantages?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Write at least 250 words.
checklist: Explain the advantages of taking a gap year (work and/or travel)
Explain the disadvantages
State clearly whether the advantages outweigh the disadvantages
Support ideas with explanations and examples
Keep the judgement consistent and restate it in the conclusion

for: Students gain maturity, independence and a clearer idea of what they want to study
Work experience develops practical skills and improves future CVs
Earning money can reduce student debt later
Travel builds language skills and understanding of other cultures
against: Students may lose study habits and find it hard to return to academic work
Some never go back to education
Travelling can be expensive, so gap years may favour wealthier families
Graduating and starting a career one year later

models.text:
In countries such as the United Kingdom and Australia, it has become increasingly common for school leavers to spend a year working or travelling before they begin university. Although this choice involves certain risks, I believe that, for most young people who plan it carefully, the benefits clearly outweigh the drawbacks.

The most significant advantage is personal growth. Many eighteen-year-olds have spent their entire lives in a structured school environment, and a year of earning a wage, managing a budget or navigating a foreign country forces them to become independent and resourceful. This maturity often pays off at university: students who have had time to reflect are more likely to choose a course that genuinely interests them, and therefore less likely to drop out or change subjects. A gap year can also be financially sensible, since a student who works for twelve months may save enough to reduce the debt they would otherwise accumulate.

There are, admittedly, some genuine disadvantages. After a year away from books and exams, some students find it difficult to readjust to academic routines, and a small minority become so attached to their income or their travels that they never return to education. In addition, an expensive trip abroad is simply not affordable for many families, so the experience can reinforce social inequality. Finally, gap-year students enter the job market a year later than their peers.

However, most of these problems can be avoided with planning. Universities in many countries allow applicants to defer their place, which guarantees that they have something to return to, and a gap year need not involve costly travel at all: working in a local business or volunteering can be just as valuable. The loss of a single year, meanwhile, is trivial over a working life of four decades.

In conclusion, provided it has a clear purpose, a gap year offers maturity, practical experience and a sense of direction that more than compensate for its potential downsides.
models.commentary: Task Response (8): juicio claro ('the benefits clearly outweigh the drawbacks') con una condición razonable ('for most young people who plan it carefully'). Ventajas y desventajas bien desarrolladas, y el cuarto párrafo responde a las desventajas, lo cual refuerza la valoración. Coherence & Cohesion (8): progresión muy lógica; 'admittedly', 'However', 'meanwhile' y la referencia ('these problems', 'this maturity') dan fluidez. Lexical Resource (8): léxico preciso ('school leavers', 'resourceful', 'drop out', 'defer their place', 'trivial', 'reinforce social inequality'). Grammatical Range & Accuracy (8): estructuras variadas ('so attached... that', 'provided it has', comparativas) sin errores. Para un 9: un ejemplo más personal o concreto (un tipo de voluntariado, un caso real) para dar aún más peso a los argumentos.

models.text:
In many Western countries, a lot of students decide to take a gap year after leaving school, which means spending a year working or travelling before going to university. In my opinion, the advantages of this experience are greater than the disadvantages.

Firstly, a gap year helps young people to become more mature and independent. When they travel alone or work in a real job, they have to make their own decisions and solve problems without help from their parents. For example, a student who works in a café for a year learns how to deal with customers, manage money and work as part of a team. These skills will be useful both at university and in their future career. Secondly, many students are not sure what they want to study when they finish school. A year off gives them time to think, so they can choose the right degree and avoid changing course later.

However, there are also some disadvantages. Some students lose the habit of studying and find it hard to go back to university. Others may enjoy working and earning money so much that they decide not to continue their education. In addition, travelling around the world is expensive, and not every family can pay for it.

Nevertheless, I believe these problems are not very serious. Students do not need to travel abroad; they can work in their own town and save money for university. Moreover, if they plan their year well, they are more motivated when they start their studies.

In conclusion, although a gap year has some risks, I think that the benefits for students' maturity, skills and future choices are more important.

Algún argumento queda poco desarrollado ('they are more motivated' sin explicación). Grammatical Range & Accuracy (7): buena variedad ('so much that', relativas, condicional) y apenas errores. Para subir a 8: desarrollar cada idea un paso más (consecuencia y ejemplo), usar léxico más específico ('defer a place', 'drop out', 'school leavers') y reducir la dependencia de conectores al inicio de frase.

In some countries the students take a year off after the school and before the university. They use this year for work or for travel. I think this has more advantages than disadvantages.

The first advantage is that the students can have experience. If they work, they learn how is the real world and how to earn money. This is very useful for the future because the companies prefer people with experience. Also if they travel, they can know new countries and new cultures and they can practise other languages like English or French. This is a very good experience for the young people. When I was eighteen I went to Ireland for three months and my English improve a lot.

The second advantage is that the students can rest. After many years in the school they are very tired and stressed, and they need a break. When they start the university they will be more relaxed and they will study better.

However, there are also some disadvantages. The students can forget the things they learned in the school. Also, travel is very expensive and not all the families have money for this, so only the rich students can do it. Some students maybe don't want to go back to study because they like to work and have money.

In conclusion, I think that take a year off has more advantages than disadvantages because the students can have experience and rest. But it is important that they make a good plan for this year and they don't forget to study after.
models.commentary: Task Response (6): postura clara y relevante, con un ejemplo personal (Irlanda), pero los argumentos son generales ('can have experience', 'can rest') y no explica por qué las ventajas pesan más que las desventajas. Coherence & Cohesion (6): organización reconocible pero mecánica ('The first advantage', 'The second advantage', 'Also', 'However'). Lexical Resource (6): vocabulario básico y repetitivo ('the students', 'experience', 'very'); errores de colocación ('know new countries' → get to know / visit). Grammatical Range & Accuracy (6): errores frecuentes: 'they learn how is the real world' (what the real world is like), 'my English improve', 'take a year off has' (taking), 'maybe don't want' (orden), artículos sobrantes ('the school', 'the university', 'the students'). Para subir a 7: desarrollar cada ventaja con una consecuencia concreta, valorar explícitamente ambos lados y trabajar preguntas indirectas, gerundio como sujeto y artículos.

prompt:
In many countries, the number of children who are overweight is increasing.

What problems does this cause? What measures could be taken to solve them?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Write at least 250 words.
checklist: Explain the problems caused by childhood obesity (for children, families and/or society)
Propose specific, realistic solutions
Link each solution to a cause or problem you have described
Support ideas with explanation and examples
Answer BOTH questions with roughly equal development

for: Problem: higher risk of diabetes, heart disease and joint problems later in life
Problem: bullying, low self-esteem and mental health issues
Problem: rising costs for public health systems
Problem: unhealthy habits formed in childhood tend to continue into adulthood
against: Solution: taxes on sugary drinks and restrictions on junk-food advertising aimed at children
Solution: healthier school meals and daily physical education
Solution: cooking and nutrition lessons for children and parents
Solution: safe parks, cycle lanes and sports facilities in neighbourhoods

models.text:
Childhood obesity has risen sharply over the past few decades, particularly in wealthy and rapidly developing countries. This trend creates serious difficulties for the children themselves and for society as a whole, but a combination of government regulation and changes in schools could do much to reverse it.

The most obvious consequences concern health. Overweight children are far more likely to develop type 2 diabetes, high blood pressure and joint problems, conditions that were once seen almost exclusively in middle-aged adults. Equally damaging, though less visible, is the psychological impact: children who are teased about their weight often suffer from low self-esteem and may withdraw from sport and social activities, which in turn makes the problem worse. Moreover, because eating habits formed in childhood tend to persist, today's overweight children are likely to become tomorrow's chronically ill adults, placing an enormous burden on public health systems.

Addressing the issue requires action on several fronts. Governments can make unhealthy choices less attractive by taxing sugary drinks, as Mexico and the United Kingdom have done, and by banning advertisements for junk food during children's television programmes. At the same time, schools have a crucial role to play, since children eat at least one meal a day there. Replacing processed food in canteens with fresh, balanced meals and guaranteeing daily physical activity would make a measurable difference. Practical cooking lessons could also equip children, and indirectly their parents, with the skills to prepare healthy food at home.

Finally, urban planning should not be overlooked. Children who live near safe parks and cycle paths are more likely to play outside, so local authorities should ensure that such spaces are available in every neighbourhood, especially in poorer areas.

In conclusion, rising childhood obesity threatens both individual well-being and the sustainability of healthcare. Tackling it effectively will require governments, schools and families to work together to make the healthy option the easy option.
models.commentary: Task Response (8): responde a ambas preguntas con desarrollo equilibrado; los problemas abarcan salud física, salud mental y coste social, y las soluciones son concretas, realistas y vinculadas a los problemas (impuestos, comedores, urbanismo). Ejemplos específicos (México, Reino Unido). Coherence & Cohesion (8): progresión clara; 'Equally damaging, though less visible', 'At the same time', 'Finally' estructuran el texto con naturalidad. Lexical Resource (8): léxico preciso ('type 2 diabetes', 'withdraw from', 'chronically ill', 'burden', 'on several fronts', 'make the healthy option the easy option'). Grammatical Range & Accuracy (8): estructuras complejas variadas (relativas reducidas, inversión de 'Equally damaging... is', condicional) sin errores. Para un 9: algo más de profundidad en el papel de las familias, que sólo se menciona de pasada, y una idea más original.

models.text:
In recent years, the number of overweight children has increased in many parts of the world. This essay will explain the main problems that this causes and suggest some possible solutions.

The first problem is related to health. Children who are overweight have a higher risk of developing serious illnesses, such as diabetes and heart disease, when they grow up. They may also have problems with their bones and joints because of the extra weight. Another problem is psychological. Overweight children are often teased by their classmates, which can make them feel unhappy and lonely. As a result, some of them avoid playing sports, so they become even less active. Finally, this situation is expensive for society, because governments have to spend more money on treating these illnesses in the future.

There are several measures that could help to solve this problem. Firstly, schools should offer healthier meals and include more physical education in the timetable. For example, in Japan, school lunches are carefully planned by nutritionists, and the rate of childhood obesity is relatively low. Secondly, governments could introduce a tax on sugary drinks and fast food to make them less attractive. Thirdly, parents need to be educated about nutrition, because they decide what their children eat at home. Information campaigns on television and social media could help them to make better choices.

In conclusion, childhood obesity causes health, emotional and economic problems. However, if schools, governments and parents work together, it is possible to reduce the number of overweight children in the future.
models.commentary: Task Response (7): responde a las dos preguntas con ideas relevantes y un buen ejemplo (Japón). Las soluciones son adecuadas pero se presentan como lista, con un desarrollo algo limitado (el impuesto se menciona sin explicar su efecto). Coherence & Cohesion (7): organización clara; uso algo mecánico de conectores ordinales ('The first problem', 'Another problem', 'Finally', 'Firstly', 'Secondly', 'Thirdly'). Lexical Resource (7): vocabulario adecuado ('teased', 'joints', 'nutritionists', 'information campaigns'), aunque con alguna expresión general ('better choices'). Grammatical Range & Accuracy (7): frases complejas correctas (relativas, 'As a result', condicional), errores casi inexistentes. Para subir a 8: desarrollar menos soluciones pero con más profundidad (cómo y por qué funcionan), conectar explícitamente soluciones con problemas y emplear conectores menos enumerativos.

models.text:
Nowadays, there are more and more children who are overweight in many countries. This is a big problem for the children and for the society. In this essay I will explain the problems and give some solutions.

First of all, being overweight is bad for the health. The children who are fat can have many illness like diabetes or problems with the heart. Also they get tired very fast and they can not play sports with their friends. Sometimes the other children laugh at them in the school and they feel sad and they don't want to go to school. This is very bad for their future.

Another problem is that the children eat a lot of fast food and sweets. Nowadays the parents are very busy and they don't have time to cook, so they buy food in the supermarket that is not healthy. Also the children play video games all the day and they don't do exercise.

There are some solutions for this problem. Firstly, the schools must to give healthy food to the children and more hours of sport. Secondly, the parents should cook more at home and don't give to the children too much sweets. Finally, the government can make advertisings to explain that the fast food is bad for the health.

In conclusion, overweight children is a serious problem in the world today. The schools, the parents and the government should work together to solve this problem and the children can be more healthy in the future.
models.commentary: Task Response (6): responde a ambas preguntas, pero el segundo párrafo del cuerpo describe causas (comida rápida, videojuegos), no problemas, lo cual desvía parcialmente la respuesta. Las soluciones se enumeran sin desarrollo. Coherence & Cohesion (6): estructura reconocible, pero enlaces mecánicos y repetitivos ('Also', 'Firstly', 'Secondly', 'Finally'); dentro de los párrafos las ideas se encadenan con 'and'. Lexical Resource (6): vocabulario básico ('bad for the health', 'very fast', 'fat' es informal y poco adecuado); errores de forma ('many illness', 'advertisings', 'all the day'). Grammatical Range & Accuracy (6): errores frecuentes: 'must to give', 'don't give... too much sweets' (not give... too many sweets), 'overweight children is', 'more healthy'; exceso de artículos ('the society', 'the health'). Para subir a 7: distinguir causas de problemas (responde a lo que se pregunta), desarrollar cada solución explicando cómo funcionaría y revisar plurales incontables y modales.
